extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers, insurers, health programs and activities), compliance/legal staff, accessibility coordinators, and OCR reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluative criteria under Section 1557 (§§ 92.201–92.202 and related provisions) for providing meaningful language access and effective communication in health programs and activities, including interpreter/translator standards, remote interpreting (VRI/audio), machine translation, companions, and procedures/training. Focus is on what covered entities must do and what OCR will consider when assessing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural competency and accuracy as necessary components of meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural competency is essential for equitable language access and communications; due to dialects, expressions, and regionalisms, cultural competency is a key factor in providing accurate interpretation and translation, and accuracy is a necessary component of meaningful access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes community-based interpreters may be more culturally competent but declines to require interpreters/translators be from the community. Covered entities may hire or contract as they see fit so long as individuals meet definitions/requirements in §92.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities may set hiring/contracting processes (subject to §92.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are free to determine their own hiring and contracting processes for utilizing the services of qualified interpreters and translators, and hiring bilingual/multilingual staff, as long as these individuals meet the requirements for their respective positions as provided in §92.4 (Definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to mandate community-membership as a requirement; compliance depends on meeting §92.4 definitions and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine translation—limited, error-prone, and subject to human review
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine translation is an evolving technology with significant potential for error; it 'means automated translation . . . that is text based and provides instant translations between various languages,' including speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR permits limited use (e.g., exigent/urgent circumstances) but requires that machine translation used in urgent circumstances be subsequently checked by a qualified human translator 'as soon as practicable.' For non-human-reviewed uses that do not meet §92.201(c)(3) criteria, OCR recommends warning patients that machine translation may contain errors. OCR balances convenience/cost against critical nature of health communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's factors for evaluating compliance (replacement for four-factor test)
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.201(d)(1) allows the Director to consider a range of relevant factors including 'the nature and importance of the health program or activity and the particular communication at issue, to the individual with limited English proficiency.' §92.201(d)(2) permits consideration of 'other relevant factors' including whether 'reasonable steps' were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider factors such as geographic location and timing (e.g., midnight in a rural area vs. urban setting) in assessing whether reasonable steps were taken; the approach is intended to be more precise and flexible than the prior four‑factor test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reliance on certain unqualified persons to interpret
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR includes an explicit prohibition on the use of certain persons to interpret or facilitate communication; reliance on accompanying adults or minors should generally be temporary and limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untrained interpreters (family, friends, minors) are more likely to make errors, violate confidentiality, and increase risk of poor outcomes; research documents omissions, additions, substitutions, volunteered opinions, semantic errors, and other problematic practices, especially with children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency/exigent exceptions for temporary reliance on non-qualified interpreters
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §92.201(e)(2)(i), a covered entity may rely on an adult not qualified as an interpreter as a temporary measure in an emergency pending the retention of a qualified interpreter; the rule was revised to allow reliance on bilingual/multilingual staff (not only accompanying adults) as a temporary measure in emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified interpreters who are bilingual staff may be used in any situation. Covered entities should obtain a qualified interpreter as quickly as possible in emergency/exigent circumstances and only rely upon other persons in highly exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions limiting use of accompanying adult as interpreter (affirmative, private request)
rubrics_metrics.description: An accompanying adult may interpret or facilitate communication only at the affirmative and independent request of the individual with LEP; such a request must be made without the accompanying adult present and with the services of a qualified interpreter (except in exigent circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities must consider whether reliance on the accompanying adult is appropriate (ability to convey information, conflicts/bias such as intimate partner violence). The rule protects autonomy and prevents coercion; a one-time request does not permit assumption that the adult will be used in future encounters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providers may use qualified interpreter despite patient's request for family/friend in safety/accuracy concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provider believes a family member/friend may not be accurately communicating, appears to be struggling, or there are good-faith suspicions of trafficking or abuse, the provider should be able to utilize a qualified interpreter even if the patient requested otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances patient autonomy with safety and accuracy concerns; the private-request requirement for accompanying adults helps protect victims/survivors of domestic/sexual violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter ethics and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: A key component of the definition of 'qualified interpreter for an individual with limited English proficiency' is adherence to generally accepted interpreter ethics principles, including client confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities subject to HIPAA and section 1557 must comply with requirements of both laws when providing interpreters and translators.

rubrics_metrics.name: VRI parity and minimum quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule reinstates VRI standards from the 2016 Rule; when video remote interpreting (VRI) is used for individuals with LEP it must meet minimum quality standards and provide meaningful access—achieving parity with VRI requirements for people with disabilities (§92.201(f) & §92.202).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality expectations include high-quality picture, video, and transmissible audio; VRI must allow for meaningful access. OCR recognizes VRI is not always appropriate and does not require covered entities to provide VRI, only that when used it meet standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for VRI technical standards in disasters/low-connectivity areas
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR recognizes that in natural disasters or locations without high-speed wide-bandwidth connections, covered entities may not meet VRI technical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such circumstances, reasonable steps to achieve meaningful access may include using qualified interpreters via telephone or in-person if available. OCR will consider specific facts when assessing whether covered entities took reasonable steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for individual's preference for modality when reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities should follow an individual's preference with respect to interpreter services where appropriate (e.g., some patients prefer telephonic interpretation to video).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to change the VRI requirements but allows covered entities to use audio-only interpretation as a reasonable step to provide meaningful access, including when it is the expressed preference of the individual with LEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: VRI operational expectations and no mandated availability timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged requirements such as connecting to a qualified interpreter within five minutes and 24-hour trained personnel; OCR requires language assistance services be provided in a timely manner but declines to mandate a specific time period for interpreter availability once a VRI device is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule requires covered entities to maintain language access procedures per §92.8(d) and to provide adequate training to users of the technology per §92.201(f)(4) so personnel can set up and operate VRI efficiently. OCR encourages procurement policies but declines to mandate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio remote interpreting must allow meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: When a covered entity uses audio remote interpreting services, it 'must ensure the modality allows for meaningful access.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes audio-only interpretation may be a poor substitute for VRI or in-person interpreting in some contexts but permits its use when it is the only or reasonable option; additional restrictions were declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coercing individuals to decline language assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity may not coerce an individual with LEP to decline language assistance services; similarly it may not require an individual to accept such services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reiterates protection of individuals' rights and prevents discouraged exercise of language access rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide auxiliary aids and services for individuals with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide appropriate auxiliary aids and services to individuals with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills, where necessary to afford such individuals an equal opportunity to benefit from the service in question (§92.202(b)), incorporating 28 CFR 35.130 and 35.160–35.164 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR requires effective communication for individuals with disabilities and their companions; auxiliary aids/services should be accurate, timely, and protect privacy/independent decision-making (commenters requested explicit parity with §92.201(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and maintain effective communication procedures and training
rubrics_metrics.description: All covered entities are required to develop and maintain effective communication procedures per §92.8(e) and to train relevant employees on these procedures per §92.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR encourages including necessary billing codes in procedures as a best practice. Training and documented procedures are intended to proactively address noncompliance and lack of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing companions unless confidentiality concerns exist; limited reliance for interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the covered entity has a specific confidentiality concern regarding a companion, the individual with a disability should be permitted to select a companion and have them present; companions can be essential for effective communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, covered entities may not rely on a person accompanying an individual with a disability to interpret or facilitate communication except when the individual specifically requests and agrees to the arrangement and it is appropriate under the circumstances (per 28 CFR 35.160(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on VRI effectiveness and prohibition on exclusive-use policies
rubrics_metrics.description: VRI may not provide effective communication in certain situations (e.g., patient limited ability to move head/hands/arms, vision or cognitive issues, significant pain, space limitations, complexity of medical issue, deafblind individuals, lying on back during procedures). Policies that require exclusive use of VRI or any single auxiliary aid/service are likely to fail to provide effective communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement and settlement agreements have found VRI ineffective in particular circumstances; covered entities should not adopt policies mandating exclusive use of VRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect patient preference on interpreter gender when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR recommends consideration of a patient's preference for the gender of the interpreter whenever possible, including for religious reasons, but declined to require such language in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether communication is effective does not inherently depend on satisfying gender preference, but honoring preference is recommended practice and some organizations urge honoring such preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage documenting accessibility needs as a best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR recognizes best practice of affirmatively asking patients what they need to make documents accessible and documenting that need so it need not be repeatedly asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR encourages covered entities to implement documentation of access needs in the written effective communication procedures required under §92.8(e), but declined to require documentation by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide auxiliary aids/services when needed (cost and billing considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: All covered entities must provide auxiliary aids and services when needed to communicate effectively with people with disabilities; commenters recommended mechanisms (e.g., state medical communication access funds) to spread costs, but OCR declined to create such state requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR encourages creative approaches and inclusion of billing codes in procedures; it reiterates that cost concerns are not a license to deny required aids/services.
